description:
Kernel auto-selection v2 is a Serving Runtime Performance project to ship improved GPU kernel selection logic that chooses the best attention/prefill/decode kernels based on (1) model family (architecture + key flags like grouped-query attention), (2) effective sequence length / prompt length buckets (prefill vs decode regimes), and (3) GPU type/SKU (e.g., L4, A10, A100, H100; and relevant SM capabilities). The goal is to improve p50/p95 latency and throughput while reducing performance variance and avoiding regressions when new model families or GPU generations are introduced.

Goals:
- Improve p95 latency and cost/token for mixed workloads by selecting kernels that match the runtime regime (short vs long context; prefill vs decode).
- Reduce tail-latency variance across GPU SKUs by making selection explicit and data-driven rather than heuristic-only.
- Provide safe rollout controls: feature-flagged v2 selector, deterministic fallback to v1 selector, and per-model-family overrides.
- Improve observability: record selection decisions (kernel id, selector version, model family, seq bucket, GPU) and correlate with latency/correctness signals.
- Expand regression prevention: add perf-canary gates and benchmark-lab coverage across representative prompt distributions.

Non-goals:
- Writing new kernels from scratch (this project focuses on selection and integration, not kernel development).
- Changing customer-facing API semantics.
- Large scheduler redesign (only minimal wiring needed to expose seq-length regime and batching context into selection).

Key stakeholders:
- Runtime org: Mateo Alvarez (VP Eng, Runtime) as exec sponsor; Hiro Tanaka (EM, Runtime Kernels) and Sofia Ivanova (EM, Runtime Scheduling).
- Technical leads/ICs: Noah Patel (runtime architecture), Grace Kim + Yuki Sato (kernel selection + GPU-specific behavior), Omar El-Sayed + Lena Fischer (scheduler integration + runtime instrumentation).
- Cross-functional: Connor O’Brien (Release Engineering) for release train and rollout; Allison Grant / SRE (Sean Gallagher org) for SLO guardrails and canary monitoring; Jonas Weber org for benchmark methodology and regression gating.
- Product coordination (rollout/visibility): Marissa Cole / Paula Mendes as needed for rollout policy alignment (especially if surfaced in Console or used by rollouts tooling).

Timeline (hypothetical):
- Phase 0 (2 weeks): gather baseline data, define model-family taxonomy, decide schema for kernel registry and selection table.
- Phase 1 (3–4 weeks): implement selector v2 (table-driven + rule fallback), add telemetry and debug tooling, wire runtime/scheduler signals.
- Phase 2 (2–3 weeks): benchmark across GPU matrix, build perf-canary gates, add conformance tests and “unknown model family” behavior.
- Phase 3 (2–4 weeks): staged rollout: internal canary -> 5% hosted -> 25% hosted -> dedicated opt-in -> default-on; finalize docs/runbooks and release notes.

Constraints and risks:
- Correctness: wrong kernel selection can cause silent numerical issues (NaNs) or rare shape mismatches; require conformance tests and “safe kernel set” fallback.
- Observability/cardinality: selection telemetry can explode cardinality; needs controlled labels/bucketing.
- Determinism: selection must be stable for identical inputs to avoid confusing perf analysis.
- Backward compatibility: must support older GPUs and older model metadata; unknown/partial metadata must not break serving.

Deliverables:
- Table-driven kernel selector v2 implementation (gated by config + feature flag) in the redwood runtime.
- Kernel registry schema and versioning, including model-family identifiers and seq-length buckets.
- Metrics/logging for selection decisions and downstream performance.
- Perf suite + canary gates updated; benchmark reports comparing v1 vs v2.
- Operator runbook for overrides/rollbacks; release notes for runtime version.

Fit within company context:
This project supports Redwood Inference’s differentiation around predictable latency/cost across changing hardware and model ecosystems. It directly improves production economics (throughput, cost/token) and reliability (tail-latency stability) for Hosted and Dedicated customers, while reducing operational risk during fleet/GPU transitions.

files.description: Primary design doc: selector v2 architecture, inputs (model family/seq bucket/GPU), decision flow, fallback strategy, config schema, rollout plan, and testing approach.
ADR documenting the decision to move from heuristic selection to a table-driven registry (including versioning strategy, ownership, and update process).
Benchmark plan and methodology: prompt distributions, model set, GPU matrix, metrics to report (p50/p95, tok/s, cost), and acceptance thresholds.
Profiling/debug playbook: how to confirm which kernel was selected, how to reproduce selection locally, and how to interpret selector telemetry in traces.
Known issues and edge cases: missing model metadata, seq-length estimation errors, GPU capability detection quirks, and mitigation/fallback guidance.
Runtime architecture page describing kernel registry, model-family taxonomy (e.g., Llama-family, Mistral-family, Qwen-family), and how metadata is sourced/validated.
SRE guardrails for rollout: SLO monitors, alert thresholds, error budget policy, and rollback criteria specific to selector v2.
Operational runbook: how to disable selector v2, pin kernels per model family, apply emergency overrides, and validate rollback success.
Runtime release notes entry: what changed, expected performance impact, config/flag changes, and compatibility notes.
Standardization doc for kernel selection metrics/log fields, cardinality controls, and required dashboards for performance-sensitive changes.
Working kickoff notes: goals, constraints, initial open questions, ownership, and short-term milestones (less polished than Confluence).
Spreadsheet-style document capturing the proposed selection table: rows by model family + seq bucket, columns by GPU type, chosen kernel ids, and rationale.
Benchmark results rollup (tables + notes): v1 vs v2 deltas, anomalies, and links to perf-canary runs; includes a section on outliers and suspected causes.
Checklist doc used by Release Eng/SRE: prereqs, dashboards to watch, step-by-step rollout stages, and rollback triggers.
Risk register (lightweight): correctness risks, perf regression risks, unknown model family handling, and mitigation/validation tasks.
Ongoing weekly sync notes with action items and decisions; includes links to Linear tickets and PRs as they land.
Notes from an instrumentation review: which labels are allowed, bucketing strategy, and any follow-up tasks to reduce cardinality.
Retro doc after rollout: what went well, what didn’t, monitoring gaps, and follow-up backlog items.
Linear project/umbrella ticket: Kernel auto-selection v2 implementation (scope, success metrics, milestones, and links to design doc).
Define model-family taxonomy and mapping rules (including how to handle unknown/experimental architectures).
Implement selector v2 core logic (table-driven), including safe fallback to v1 and deterministic tie-breaking.
Add sequence-length bucketing signal (prefill vs decode + effective context) and integrate with scheduler/runtime boundary.
GPU capability detection + normalization (SKU mapping, SM capability, and handling MIG/partitioned environments).
Kernel registry schema + versioning (including how entries are generated, reviewed, and promoted).
Telemetry for selection decisions: metrics/events, sampling, label bucketing, and trace annotations.
Conformance tests: ensure selected kernels produce correct outputs across representative shapes; add NaN/overflow guards.
Benchmark-lab updates to run selector v2 experiments across GPU matrix and prompt distributions; publish report artifact.
Perf-canary gate: integrate selector v2 perf thresholds into CI (fail if p95 regresses beyond defined budgets).
Runtime config/feature flag wiring: enable by tier/region, support per-model overrides, and add emergency kill switch.
Build a debug endpoint / CLI output to print “why this kernel was selected” for a given request context.
SRE dashboards + alerts updates: add selector version breakdown, kernel-choice heatmaps, and tail-latency monitors.
Rollout execution ticket: staged rollout plan, tracking, and sign-offs (runtime + SRE + release engineering).
Post-rollout follow-ups: cleanup deprecated v1-only codepaths, document update process for registry entries.
PM ticket: define customer-facing behavior/communications for selector changes (if any), and align rollout policy with model rollouts tooling.
PR implementing selector v2 core selection logic and interfaces; includes unit tests and initial registry loading.
PR adding model-family detection/mapping based on model metadata; includes fallback behavior for unknown families.
PR wiring sequence-length buckets from scheduler into kernel selection context; includes perf impact notes.
PR adding GPU SKU normalization and capability detection used by selector v2; includes tests for known GPU types.
PR introducing kernel registry schema + versioning and a small initial table for top model families.
PR adding feature flag/kill switch and per-model-family overrides, plus config validation.
PR adding selection decision telemetry (metrics + trace annotations) with label bucketing and sampling.
PR adding correctness/conformance tests for selected kernels across representative shapes and seq buckets.

PR adding perf-canary gating thresholds and dashboards links for selector v2; includes CI integration notes.
PR adjusting telemetry label sets and aggregation to reduce cardinality after initial rollout feedback.
